cards.questionText: Analyse how changes to economic variables in the economy have effected businesses like West Shore Adventure Centre.

taskRequirements: Two variables at 8 marks each: Variable 4, Explain 2, Link 2.

detail: This is a sustained growth in the general level of prices based on the Consumer Price Index. Low inflation means: • Spending power is boosted in the local economy • Higher standard of living in the economy • Investment opportunities in the community Business Sales: This refers to a rise in the average level of prices from one period to the next. Sales decrease: When prices go up, sales decrease as consumers will not be able to afford more expensive services. Business Costs: Wage costs: Employers must allow wage increases in order to compensate for inflation and increases in the cost of living. If inflation is low, i.e. price increases are minimal, this has a positive impact on a business’s costs. The cost of running expenses, raw materials etc will not increase dramatically. Inflation is rising in Ireland by soaring energy costs. Business Confidence Low business confidence: Businesses are less likely to invest and expand due to uncertainty over possible economic crashes. Link: “surging costs has highlighted the need to raise prices in order to reach their profit forecasts”.

This is the cost of borrowing. It depends on the demand and supply of money and is measured as a percentage. A low interest rate means that it is cheap for firms to borrow money. • They will expand, creating jobs • Consumers will borrow and spend • Firms are more profitable This boosts the local economy as the cost of credit is lower for consumers and investors. Business Sales: If interest rates are low, this has a positive impact on Irish businesses as sales increase. Business Costs: This refers to the cost of borrowing capital. The interest charged on loans/borrowings from financial institutions. Business Confidence: A decrease in interest rates leads to more consumer borrowing. Consumers will use borrowed finance to pay for houses, cars, furniture etc. COVID-19 Business Loans up to €25,000 usually up to 3 years, were available to sole traders, partnerships and limited companies with fewer than 10 full time employees. There are no repayments for the first 6 months and the equivalent 12 months interest-free subject to certain terms and conditions. Link: “availability of low-cost credit from financial institutions has encouraged them to expand the business”.

The unemployment rate in Ireland is 5.5%. • It is the number of people who are available and seek work unsuccessfully • Low unemployment is good for business as consumers have greater incomes and therefore greater purchasing power. It means more revenue for government and less spending on social welfare. This boosts the local economy. Business Sales When the people/the labour force have less income, consumer spending decreases. This leads to a decrease in sales for Irish businesses. Business Costs: The more unemployed people there are, the more money the government has to pay out to them in social welfare benefits. This forces the government to increase taxes to be able to afford these extra payments. Business Confidence When the labour force have less income, this refers to the percentage of the labour force who are engaged in paid employment. A decrease in employment levels has a negative impact on Irish businesses. A lot of people (employees and self-employed) became unemployed during the pandemic and were in receipt of the Pandemic Unemployment Payment (PUP). As a result a lot of non-essential business activity was stopped for a duration of time while restrictions were in place. Link: “As a result of national restrictions and high unemployment rates, bookings decreased”

Governments use taxation to: • Run the country, e.g. hospitals • Encourage businesses to change behaviour, e.g. carbon tax on fossil fuels Business Sales: Lower tax rates lead to increased sales and profits and boost the local economy as employees have more disposable income Business Costs: Cost of doing business in Ireland increases when tax rates are higher Business Confidence: The tax collected can be redistributed through transfer payments/social welfare payments/pandemic supports. During the pandemic businesses were faced with financial difficulties and the government offered various financial supports to businesses to help them overcome the financial issues associated with the closures. Link: “To survive the business had to avail of government supports during the pandemic”

detail: This includes issues such as persistent lateness, and absenteeism either short-term or long-term. The employer will be expected to have documentary proof of this allegation, such as clocking-in records or documented absences on file that are not medically certified. In addition, your employer will also be expected to show that you were made aware of the problem and that you were warned as to the consequences for your continued employment.

Incompetence refers to your inability to do your job (poor work performance/failure to meet sales targets). In the first place, you need to be made aware of the standards that are expected of you, and these must refer to the job you were hired to do. Secondly, if you fall short of the required standard, this must be clearly explained to you. This should be done through a formal set of procedure. cards.questionText: Describe the role of the Workplace Relations Commission in dealing with industrial relations disputes.

rubric.markingGuideNote: The official support notes give possible responses, not an exhaustive list. Other relevant answers are considered on their merits. Apply the published allocation to your answer; do not count the same point twice.

detail: The Workplace Relations Commission’s Advisory Service promotes good practice in the workplace by assisting and advising organisations on all aspects of industrial relations in the workplace. It works with employers, employees and their representatives to help them to develop effective industrial relations practices, procedures and structures. Such assistance could include reviewing or developing effective workplace procedures in areas such as grievances, discipline, communications and consultation.

Conciliation is a voluntary process in which the parties to a dispute agree to avail of a neutral and impartial third party to assist them in resolving their industrial relations differences. The Workplace Relations Commission provides a conciliation service by making available Industrial Relations Officers (IRO or Conciliation Officer) of the Commission to chair ‘conciliation conferences’. Conciliation conferences are basically an extension of the process of direct negotiations, with an independent chairperson present to steer the discussions and explore possible avenues of settlement in a nonprejudicial fashion. Participation in the conciliation process is voluntary, and so too are the outcomes. Solutions are reached only by consensus, whether by negotiation and agreements facilitated between the parties themselves, or by the parties agreeing to settlement terms proposed by the Conciliation Officer.

Mediation seeks to arrive at a solution through an agreement between the parties, rather than through an investigation or hearing or formal decision. The WRC offers a mediation service in certain cases to facilitate the resolution of complaints/disputes where possible at an early stage and without recourse to adjudication. The Mediation Officer empowers the parties to negotiate their own agreement on a clear and informed basis. The process is voluntary and either party may terminate it at any stage. Where an attempt at mediation has been successful, the mediation officer will record the terms of the agreement in writing. If each of the parties are satisfied that the record accurately represents the terms of the resolution, they will sign the record.

Adjudication Officers of the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC) are statutorily independent in their decision-making duties. The Adjudication Officer’s role is to hold a hearing where both parties are given an opportunity to be heard by the Adjudication Officer and to present any evidence relevant to the complaint. The Adjudication Officer will not attempt to mediate or conciliate the case. The Adjudication Officer will then decide the matter and give a written decision in relation to the complaint. A party to a complaint may appeal to the Labour Court about a decision of an Adjudication Officer.

Inspectors visit places of employment and carry out investigations on behalf of the WRC in order to ensure compliance with equality and employment-related legislation. Such investigations involve examining books, records and documents related to the employment, and conducting interviews with current and former employees and employers. Where breaches of legislation have been found, an Inspector may issue either a Compliance Notice or a Fixed Payment Notice to an employer.

detail: This refers to expansion achieved naturally within the business itself. Organic growth is slow and it happens gradually with time. Shareholders reinvest profits to fund expansion. It does not involve outside firms. Examples: increase sales at home or abroad, franchising, licensing

(ii) Discuss the reasons, other than increasing profit, for expansion of a business.

guidance: The scheme restates (ii) as “Discuss reasons, other than increasing profit, why entrepreneurs expand their business.”; the card follows the paper.
rubric.markingGuideNote: The official support notes give possible responses, not an exhaustive list. Other relevant answers are considered on their merits. Apply the published allocation to your answer; do not count the same point twice.

detail: A business may want to grow to benefit from economies of scale. This will reduce the unit cost of production. Products become cheaper and the business can become more competitive in the market. In order to protect supplies, a business may expand by purchasing their supplier. This is known as backward vertical integration. The business is guaranteed access to all their supplies at cost price. To defend itself from possible market saturation or competition, a business may diversify. This involves entering into an entirely different market. The business may purchase another firm or start providing a product or service in a completely unrelated area. This helps to spread the risk of failure in one particular market. To ensure constant distribution, a business may expand by buying out the retailer which sells its products. This is called forward vertical integration. This guarantees a constant market for its products.

A business may wish to eliminate competition and be the dominant player in a market. By taking over competitors, this ensures the largest market share for the business. Entrepreneurs may see an opportunity to acquire a business to access a new product. It may be cheaper for the business to acquire the company than attempt to develop a competing product. Some businesses are bought out by entrepreneurs in order to asset strip. The entrepreneur sees an opportunity to maximise profits by selling off the acquired firm’s assets for more than the business cost.

Many entrepreneurs are motivated by the challenge of setting up new businesses. They are successful in their original business but enjoy the challenge of starting in new markets or acquiring other firms. Entrepreneurs are ambitious by nature. They may want to be the most successful in their industry or make a lot of money. They may want to build an empire and expand in order to do this.

rubric.markingGuideNote: The official support notes give possible responses, not an exhaustive list. Other relevant answers are considered on their merits. Apply the published allocation to your answer; do not count the same point twice.

detail: Initial ideas for the new product are thought up systematically. They can be internal or external. Ideas may be generated by market research, staff suggestions, customer suggestions/feedback on existing products or services, competitors, R&D etc. Gym+Coffee may hold brainstorming sessions to identify new product ideas.

All ideas are vetted and the impractical and unworkable ideas are dropped, leaving the most viable ones for further examination and development. Careful screening helps businesses avoid huge expenses in developing ideas that are subsequently not marketable and ensures that good opportunities are not lost. Gym+Coffee may conduct a SWOT analysis to identify the idea with the most potential.

This involves turning the idea into an actual product or service that will appeal to/meet the needs of customers. A unique selling point (USP) is identified which will differentiate it from other products on the market. Gym+Coffee may identify the USP of recycled material for its new product.

This is carried out to assess if a product has potential. It looks at whether it can be produced technically (production feasibility) and if it will be profitable (financial feasibility). It seeks answers to questions such as, what demand there will be for the product; what will it cost to produce and can the business afford it? Gym+Coffee will conduct a detailed cost analysis to determine the feasibility of the new product.

cards.questionText: Contrast Debt Capital and Equity Capital as sources of finance for business expansion.

rubric.markingGuideNote: The official support notes give possible responses, not an exhaustive list. Other relevant answers are considered on their merits. Apply the published allocation to your answer; do not count the same point twice.

detail: Debt capital must be repaid with interest over the lifetime of the loan. A debenture usually involves making interest payments throughout the loan period and the capital amount is repaid in the final year. There is no interest charged with equity capital.
Equity capital does not have to be repaid. Share capital is only ever repaid if the company is being wound up (closed down). The entire loan/debt must be repaid in full with interest.

Debt capital repayments reduce tax liability for the business. Interest repayments on the loan are an expense of the business, which reduces net profit, therefore, reducing corporation tax paid. There are no tax benefits from equity capital.

The ownership of a business is not affected if it uses debt capital. Equity capital involves selling shares in the business. Each share sold dilutes control of the business as the shareholders are now part owners of the business.

A business must provide collateral for a loan. This is also known as security on the loan and an asset is used. In the event of the loan not being repaid, the asset will not be seized. Equity capital does not have to provide collateral.

If the business fails to repay the debt, it runs the risk of being declared bankrupt and the business will cease to operate. There is less risk involved with equity capital as there is no requirement to repay share capital.
